cim: CES 2027: Ambarella and Liquid AI team up on edge AI for smart infrastructure
cim_eredeti: CES 2027: Ambarella and Liquid AI team up on edge AI for smart infrastructure
szoveg_eredeti:
Liquid’s foundation models are now available in the Cooper Model Garden in the Developer Zone of Ambarella, allowing developers to build applications on Liquid models running directly on Ambarella silicon. Support for further Liquid models is planned across Ambarella’s portfolio, including the CV72, CV75 and N1-655 systems on chip (SoCs) and the X7 AI accelerator.

The joint work initially focuses on the LFM3 family of Liquid foundation models, introduced in October, and their execution on Ambarella’s CVflow AI architecture. The Liquid models are being optimised for CVflow to lower AI compute and memory utilisation.

The companies add that DRAM supply is constrained and memory prices are rising across the electronics industry. Reducing memory requirements while expanding on-device intelligence can therefore also offer system-level cost advantages, they say, including the deployment of more capable AI systems at lower overall hardware cost and with improved power efficiency.

The two companies are optimising an intelligence stack intended to let physical AI systems go beyond conventional perception and inference. The aim is for such systems to reason across multimodal inputs, make decisions, execute actions and verify outcomes locally, without relying on continuous cloud connectivity.

“Physical AI represents a fundamental evolution in artificial intelligence, where intelligence moves beyond centralized data centers and into the devices that interact directly with the physical world,” says Muneyb Minhazuddin, customer growth officer at Ambarella. “These systems must do much more than recognize objects or process individual sensor inputs. They must understand context, reason about their environment, make decisions and take actions in real time.”

He adds: “Our collaboration with Liquid AI brings together highly efficient foundation models with Ambarella’s purpose-built, power-efficient edge AI architecture. By optimizing the hardware and software stack, we are working to deliver a new level of multimodal intelligence and autonomy directly on edge devices.”

The companies are initially targeting physical AI applications, such as intelligent security and smart infrastructure, that need to interpret complex visual and contextual information, understand changing conditions, make autonomous decisions and respond in real time.

“Equally important, we are addressing the economics of Physical AI by enabling increasingly sophisticated AI capabilities within significantly constrained memory, power and system-cost budgets,” Minhazuddin continues. “This combination has the potential to accelerate the deployment of intelligent systems across Physical AI markets.”

Liquid AI says its products extend beyond individual foundation models to include the software infrastructure needed to deploy and operate autonomous AI agents. Its foundation models and agent harness are designed to work together, so that agents can continuously interpret information, reason about their environment, determine appropriate actions and verify outcomes.

Through what it calls a co-design approach, Liquid works with enterprise customers to optimise both the models and the agent harness for specific applications and hardware platforms. This allows physical AI systems to combine multimodal perception, contextual understanding, reasoning and action while maintaining awareness over time. According to the companies, running these capabilities locally can provide greater responsiveness, privacy and operational resilience, while reducing reliance on cloud-based inference.

“Bringing agentic AI into the physical world requires a fundamentally different approach to AI architecture,” says Erika Wool, head of business at Liquid AI. “Intelligence must operate where data is generated, with the ability to perceive, reason, remember, and act within the power, memory and latency constraints of real-world devices. By working with Ambarella, we are bringing Liquid models to their developer ecosystem and customers, with support across their portfolio of edge AI SoCs.”

The companies plan to show demonstrations of solutions built with Liquid’s LFM3 models on Ambarella SoCs at CES 2027.

Ambarella says its AI SoCs have an installed base of more than 50 million units, used in applications including physical security, vehicle safety, telematics, autonomy, portable video, aerial drones and robotics. Liquid describes itself as a device-native foundation model company whose open-weight foundation models are designed to run on any device with a processor.
